class Solution {
public:
    int findMaximumX(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
        int m = matrix.size();
        int n = matrix[0].size();
        int maxX = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (matrix[i][j] > maxX) {
                    maxX = matrix[i][j];
                }
            }
        }
        return maxX;
    }
};

import React from 'react';
import { useState } from 'react';
import axios from 'axios';

const API_URL = 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts';

const Posts = () => {
  const [posts, setPosts] = useState([]);

  useEffect(() => {
    axios.get(`${API_URL}?_limit=10`)
      .then(response => {
        setPosts(response.data);
      })
      .catch(error => {
        console.log(error);
      });
  }, []);

  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Posts</h1>
      <ul>
        {posts.map(post => (
          <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
};

export default Posts;

class App extends React.Component {
  state = {
    data: []
  };

  componentDidMount() {
    axios.get(`${API_URL}/data`)
      .then(response => {
        this.setState({ data: response.data });
      })
      .catch(error => {
        console.error(error);
      });
  }

  render() {
    return (
      <div>
        <h1>Data</h1>
        <ul>
          {this.state.data.map(item => (
            <li key={item.id}>{item.name}</li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </div>
    );
  }
}

export default App;

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def sigmoid(x):
    return 1 / (1 + np.exp(-x))

def derivative(x, sigmoid):
    return sigmoid * (1 - sigmoid) * x

def sigmoid_derivative(x):
    return derivative(x, sigmoid)

# Define the function space
x = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
y = sigmoid(x)

# Plot the function
plt.plot(x, y)
plt.xlabel('Input')
plt.ylabel('Output')
plt.title('Sigmoid Function')
plt.show()

# Define the derivative space
dx = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)

plt.xlabel('Input')
plt.ylabel('Derivative')

def interpolate_data(data, x_values, y_values):
    # Interpolate the data using a cubic spline
    x_interp = np.linspace(x_values[0], x_values[-1], 1000)
    y_interp = interpolate.cubic_interp(x_values, y_values, x_interp)
    return y_interp

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaximumX(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
        int m = matrix.size();
        int n = matrix[0].size();
        int maxX = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (matrix[i][j] > maxX) {
                    maxX = matrix[i][j];
                }
            }
        }
        return maxX;
    }
};

#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>

using namespace std;

int main() {
    string s;
    cin >> s;
    vector<string> words;
    for (int i = 0; i < s.size(); i++) {
        if (s[i] == ' ' || s[i] == '\n') {
            words.push_back(s.substr(i, 1));
            i++;
        }
    }
    sort(words.begin(), words.end());
    for (int i = 0; i < words.size(); i++) {
        cout << words[i] << " ";
    }
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}

// Output:
//   Hello
//   World
//   Space
//   New
//   Line

This is a simple C++ program that reads a string from the user, splits it into individual words using space or new line as the delimiter, sorts the words and then prints them back to the user.

#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>

using namespace std;

int main() {
    string s;
    cin >> s;
    vector<string> words;
    for (int i = 0; i < s.size(); i++) {
        if (s[i] == ' ' || s[i] == '\n') {
            words.push_back(s.substr(i, 1));
            i++;
        }
    }
    sort(words.begin(), words.end());
    for (int i = 0; i < words.size(); i++) {
        cout << words[i] << " ";
    }
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}

// Output:
//   Hello
//   World
//   Space
//   New
//   Line

This is a simple C++ program that reads a string from the user, splits it into individual words using space or new line as the delimiter, sorts the words and then prints them back to the user.

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaximumX(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
        int m = matrix.size();
        int n = matrix[0].size();
        int maxX = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (matrix[i][j] > maxX) {
                    maxX = matrix[i][j];
                }
            }
        }
        return maxX;
    }
};

def interpolate_data(data, x_values, y_values):
    # Interpolate the data using a cubic spline

    return y_interp

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaximumX(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
        int m = matrix.size();
        int n = matrix[0].size();
        int maxX = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (matrix[i][j] > maxX) {
                    maxX = matrix[i][j];
                }
            }
        }
        return maxX;
    }
};

def interpolate_data(data, x_values, y_values):

#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>

using namespace std;

int main() {
    string s;
    cin >> s;
    vector<string> words;
    for (int i = 0; i < s.size(); i++) {
        if (s[i] == ' ' || s[i] == '\n') {
            words.push_back(s.substr(i, 1));
            i++;
        }
    }
    sort(words.begin(), words.end());
    for (int i = 0; i < words.size(); i++) {
        cout << words[i] << " ";
    }
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}

// Output:
//   Hello
//   World
//   Space
//   New
//   Line

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaximumX(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
        int m = matrix.size();
        int n = matrix[0].size();
        int maxX = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (matrix[i][j] > maxX) {
                    maxX = matrix[i][j];
                }
            }
        }
        return maxX;
    }
};

#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>

using namespace std;

int main() {
    string s;
    cin >> s;
    vector<string> words;
    for (int i = 0; i < s.size(); i++) {
        if (s[i] == ' ' || s[i] == '\n') {
            words.push_back(s.substr(i, 1));
            i++;
        }
    }
    sort(words.begin(), words.end());
    for (int i = 0; i < words.size(); i++) {
        cout << words[i] << " ";
    }
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}

// Output:
//   Hello
//   World
//   Space
//   New
//   Line

This is a simple C++ program that reads a string from the user, splits it into individual words using space or new line as the delimiter, sorts the words and then prints them back to the user.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def sigmoid(x):
    return 1 / (1 + np.exp(-x))

def derivative(x, sigmoid):
    return sigmoid * (1 - sigmoid) * x

def sigmoid_derivative(x):
    return derivative(x, sigmoid)

plt.ylabel('Output')
plt.title('Sigmoid Function')
plt.show()

from scipy.interpolate import interpolate

def interpolate_data(data, x_values, y_values):
    # Interpolate the data using a cubic spline
    x_interp = np.linspace(x_values[0], x_values[-1], 1000)
    y_interp = interpolate.cubic_interp(x_values, y_values, x_interp)
    return y_interp

# Load the data

# Plot the original data and the interpolated data

def sigmoid(x):
    return 1 / (1 + np.exp(-x))

def derivative(x, sigmoid):
    return sigmoid * (1 - sigmoid) * x

def sigmoid_derivative(x):
    return derivative(x, sigmoid)

from scipy.interpolate import interpolate

def interpolate_data(data, x_values, y_values):
    # Interpolate the data using a cubic spline
    x_interp = np.linspace(x_values[0], x_values[-1], 1000)

    return y_interp

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaximumX(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
        int m = matrix.size();
        int n = matrix[0].size();
        int maxX = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (matrix[i][j] > maxX) {
                    maxX = matrix[i][j];
                }
            }
        }
        return maxX;
    }
};

#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>

using namespace std;

int main() {
    string s;
    cin >> s;
    vector<string> words;
    for (int i = 0; i < s.size(); i++) {
        if (s[i] == ' ' || s[i] == '\n') {
            words.push_back(s.substr(i, 1));
            i++;
        }
    }
    sort(words.begin(), words.end());
    for (int i = 0; i < words.size(); i++) {
        cout << words[i] << " ";
    }
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}

// Output:
//   Hello
//   World
//   Space
//   New
//   Line

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaximumX(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
        int m = matrix.size();
        int n = matrix[0].size();
        int maxX = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (matrix[i][j] > maxX) {
                    maxX = matrix[i][j];
                }
            }
        }
        return maxX;
    }
};

import axios from 'axios';

const API_URL = 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts';

const Posts = () => {
  const [posts, setPosts] = useState([]);

  useEffect(() => {
    axios.get(`${API_URL}?_limit=10`)
      .then(response => {
        setPosts(response.data);
      })
      .catch(error => {
        console.log(error);
      });
  }, []);

  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Posts</h1>
      <ul>
        {posts.map(post => (
          <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
};

export default Posts;

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaxForm(vector<int>& forms, int num) {
        // Write your code here
        int maxForm = forms[0];
        for (int i = 1; i < num; i++) {
            if (forms[i] > maxForm) {
                maxForm = forms[i];
            }
        }
        return maxForm;
    }
};

    vector<string> words(n);

}

import React from 'react';
import { useState } from 'react';
import axios from 'axios';

const API_URL = 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts';

const Posts = () => {
  const [posts, setPosts] = useState([]);

  const fetchPosts = async () => {
    try {
      const response = await axios.get(`${API_URL}`);
      setPosts(response.data);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(error);
    }
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    fetchPosts();
  }, []);

  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Posts</h1>
      <ul>
        {posts.map((post) => (
          <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
};

export default Posts;

```

The first sentence of a story sets the tone for the entire piece. It's your chance to hook the reader and draw them in. Here are some tips for crafting a great first sentence:
1. Start with a hook: Use a surprising or intriguing fact, a question, or a vivid image to grab the reader's attention.
2. Use active voice: Write your sentence in the present tense and use active verbs to create a sense of immediacy and action.
3. Show, don't tell: Rather than telling the reader something directly, try to show it through action, dialogue, or sensory details.
4. Be concise: Keep your first sentence short and to the point. A long, rambling sentence can be off-putting and make it harder for the reader to get into the story.
5. Use specific language: Avoid generalizations and vague descriptions. Instead, use specific language that creates a clear picture in the reader's mind.
6. Avoid clichés: Try to avoid using overused phrases or sentences that have been done many

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaxForm(vector<int>& forms, int num) {
        // Write your code here
        int maxForm = forms[0];
        for (int i = 1; i < num; i++) {
            if (forms[i] > maxForm) {
                maxForm = forms[i];
            }
        }
        return maxForm;
    }
};

function App() {
  return (
    <BrowserRouter>
      <div>
        <Switch>
          <Route path="/" exact component={Home} />
          <Route path="/about" component={About} />
          <Route path="/contact" component={Contact} />
        </Switch>
      </div>
    </BrowserRouter>
  );
}

export default App;

```

The `Link` component is used to create links between the routes. For example, the link `<Link to="/about">Learn More</Link>` will navigate the user to the `/about` route when clicked.

  };

    <div>

      <ul>
        {data.map((item, index) => (
          <li key={index}>{item}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
}

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaxForm(vector<int>& forms, int num) {
        // Write your code here
        int maxForm = forms[0];
        for (int i = 1; i < num; i++) {
            if (forms[i] > maxForm) {
                maxForm = forms[i];
            }
        }
        return maxForm;
    }
};

The first sentence of a story sets the tone for the entire piece. It's your chance to hook the reader and draw them in. Here are some tips for crafting a great first sentence:
1. Start with a hook: Use a surprising or intriguing fact, a question, or a vivid image to grab the reader's attention.
2. Use active voice: Write your sentence in the present tense and use active verbs to create a sense of immediacy and action.
3. Show, don't tell: Rather than telling the reader something directly, try to show it through action, dialogue, or sensory details.
4. Be concise: Keep your first sentence short and to the point. A long, rambling sentence can be off-putting and make it harder for the reader to get into the story.

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaxForm(vector<int>& forms, int num) {
        // Write your code here
        int maxForm = forms[0];
        for (int i = 1; i < num; i++) {
            if (forms[i] > maxForm) {
                maxForm = forms[i];
            }
        }
        return maxForm;
    }
};

The law was enacted in response to growing concerns about water pollution and its impact on public health and the environment. The Clean Water Act established the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and gave it the authority to set standards for water quality and to regulate the discharge of pollutants into the nation's waters.

class Solution {

    int findMaxForm(vector<int>& forms, int num) {
        // Write your code here
        int maxForm = forms[0];
        for (int i = 1; i < num; i++) {
            if (forms[i] > maxForm) {
                maxForm = forms[i];
            }
        }
        return maxForm;
    }

const API_URL = 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts';

function App() {
  const [posts, setPosts] = useState([]);

  const fetchPosts = async () => {
    try {
      const response = await axios.get(`${API_URL}`);
      setPosts(response.data);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(error);
    }
  };

  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Posts</h1>
      <ul>
        {posts.map((post) => (
          <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <button onClick={fetchPosts}>Fetch Posts</button>
    </div>
  );
}

export default App;

void sort(vector<int> &arr, int start, int end) {
    if (start < end) {
        int pivot = start + (end - start) / 2;
        sort(arr, start, pivot);
        sort(arr, pivot + 1, end);
        merge(arr, start, pivot, end);
    }
}

18: PPL-XL=1.199, , score=0.182




class Solution {
public:
    int findMaximumX(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
        int m = matrix.size();
        int n = matrix[0].size();
        int maxX = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (matrix[i][j] > maxX) {
                    maxX = matrix[i][j];
                }
            }
        }
        return maxX;
    }
};

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaxForm(vector<int>& nums) {
        int max = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < nums.size(); i++) {
            if (nums[i] > max) {
                max = nums[i];
            }
        }
        return max;
    }
};

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    Solution solution;
    int maxForm = solution.findMaxForm(nums);
    cout << "Max form: " << maxForm << endl;
    return 0;
}

```

This is a solution to the problem "Find the maximum form of a given vector of integers". The solution uses a simple loop to iterate through the vector and checks if the current element is greater than the maximum element found so

#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <map>
#include <set>
#include <algorithm>

using namespace std;

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaxForm(vector<int>& nums) {
        int max = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < nums.size(); i++) {
            if (nums[i] > max) {
                max = nums[i];
            }
        }
        return max;
    }
};

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    Solution solution;
    int maxForm = solution.findMaxForm(nums);
    cout << "Max form: " << maxForm << endl;
    return 0;
}

import React from 'react';
import { useState } from 'react';
import axios from 'axios';

const API_URL = 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts';

function App() {
  const [posts, setPosts] = useState([]);

  const fetchPosts = async () => {
    try {
      const response = await axios.get(`${API_URL}`);
      setPosts(response.data);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(error);
    }
  };

  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Posts</h1>
      <ul>
        {posts.map((post) => (
          <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <button onClick={fetchPosts}>Fetch Posts</button>
    </div>
  );
}

export default App;
```

void sort(vector<int> &arr, int start, int end) {
    if (start < end) {
        int pivot = start + (end - start) / 2;
        sort(arr, start, pivot);
        sort(arr, pivot + 1, end);
        merge(arr, start, pivot, end);
    }
}

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaximumX(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
        int m = matrix.size();
        int n = matrix[0].size();
        int maxX = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (matrix[i][j] > maxX) {
                    maxX = matrix[i][j];
                }
            }
        }
        return maxX;
    }
};

void sort(vector<int> &arr, int start, int end) {
    if (start < end) {
        int pivot = start + (end - start) / 2;
        sort(arr, start, pivot);
        sort(arr, pivot + 1, end);
        merge(arr, start, pivot, end);
    }
}

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaximumX(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
        int m = matrix.size();
        int n = matrix[0].size();
        int maxX = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (matrix[i][j] > maxX) {
                    maxX = matrix[i][j];
                }
            }
        }
        return maxX;
    }
};

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaxForm(vector<int>& nums) {
        int max = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < nums.size(); i++) {
            if (nums[i] > max) {
                max = nums[i];
            }
        }
        return max;
    }
};

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    Solution solution;
    int maxForm = solution.findMaxForm(nums);
    cout << "Max form: " << maxForm << endl;
    return 0;
}

# Titanosaurus

Titanosaurus (meaning "Titan lizard") is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period, around 85 to 75 million years ago. The type and only species is Titanosaurus indicus. It was described in 1979 and is known from a nearly complete skeleton found in the Kutch District of Gujarat, India.

Titanosaurus was a very large sauropod, estimated to have reached lengths of around 30 meters (98 feet) and weighing around 100 metric tons (110 tons). It had a long, heavy body with a small head, a long neck, and a long tail. Its limbs were relatively short compared to its body size, and it had five clawed digits on each foot.

Titanosaurus is known for its unique skull and dental structure. Its skull was broad and flat, with a long, curved snout and a distinctive crest on the top of the skull. Its teeth were also distinctive, with a rounded crown and a distinctive root structure

})

  private apiUrl = 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users';

  constructor(private http: HttpClient) { }

  getUsers(): Observable<User[]> {
    return this.http.get(this.apiUrl);
  }

  getUser(id: number): Observable<User> {
    return this.http.get(`${this.apiUrl}/${id}`);
  }

  createUser(user: User): Observable<User> {
    return this.http.post(this.apiUrl, user);
  }

  updateUser(user: User): Observable<User> {
    return this.http.put(`${this.apiUrl}/${user.id}`, user);

  );
}

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaximumX(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
        int m = matrix.size();
        int n = matrix[0].size();
        int maxX = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (matrix[i][j] > maxX) {
                    maxX = matrix[i][j];
                }
            }
        }
        return maxX;
    }
};

#include <algorithm>

using namespace std;

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaxForm(vector<int>& nums) {
        int max = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < nums.size(); i++) {
            if (nums[i] > max) {
                max = nums[i];
            }
        }
        return max;
    }
};

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    Solution solution;
    int maxForm = solution.findMaxForm(nums);
    cout << "Max form: " << maxForm << endl;
    return 0;
}

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Generate some random data
n = 1000
x = np.random.normal(0, 1, size=n)
y = np.random.normal(0, 2, size=n)

# Plot the data
plt.scatter(x, y)
plt.xlabel('X')
plt.ylabel('Y')
plt.title('Random Data')
plt.show()

# Calculate the correlation coefficient
corr = np.corrcoef(x, y)
print(corr)

# Plot the correlation coefficient
plt.plot(corr)
plt.xlabel('Correlation Coefficient')
plt.ylabel('Value')
plt.title('Correlation Coefficient')
plt.show()

# Calculate the p-value for the correlation coefficient
p_value = np.correlate(x, y, 'pearson')
print(p_value)

# Plot the p-value
plt.plot(p_value)

# Titanosaurus

Titanosaurus (meaning "Titan lizard") is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period, around 85 to 75 million years ago. The type and only species is Titanosaurus indicus. It was described in 1979 and is known from a nearly complete skeleton found in the Kutch District of Gujarat, India.

Titanosaurus was a very large sauropod, estimated to have reached lengths of around 30 meters (98 feet) and weighing around 100 metric tons (110 tons). It had a long, heavy body with a small head, a long neck, and a long tail. Its limbs were relatively short compared to its body size, and it had five clawed digits on each foot.

Titanosaurus is known for its unique skull and dental structure. Its skull was broad and flat, with a long, curved snout and a distinctive crest on the top of the skull. Its teeth were also distinctive, with a rounded crown and a distinctive root structure

The Myth of the "Lone Wolf" Entrepreneur
The idea of the "lone wolf" entrepreneur is a myth that has been perpetuated in popular culture. The notion that successful entrepreneurs are solitary figures who work alone, without any support or guidance, has been debunked by research and real-world examples. In reality, most successful entrepreneurs rely on a network of mentors, advisors, and peers to help them navigate the challenges of starting and growing a business.

#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>

using namespace std;

int main() {
    int n;
    cin >> n;
    vector<string> names(n);
    vector<int> ages(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        string name;
        int age;
        cin >> name >> age;
        names[i] = name;
        ages[i] = age;
    }
    sort(names.begin(), names.end());
    sort(ages.begin(), ages.end());
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        cout << names[i] << " is " << ages[i] << " years old." << endl;
    }
    return 0;
}

```

This is a C++ program that reads in `n` names and ages from the user, stores them in a vector of strings and a vector of integers, sorts the vectors, and then prints out each name and age in a separate line

void sort(vector<int> &arr, int start, int end) {
    if (start < end) {
        int pivot = start + (end - start) / 2;
        sort(arr, start, pivot);
        sort(arr, pivot + 1, end);
        merge(arr, start, pivot, end);
    }
}

using namespace std;

int main() {
    int n;
    cin >> n;
    vector<string> names(n);
    vector<int> ages(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        string name;
        int age;
        cin >> name >> age;
        names[i] = name;
        ages[i] = age;
    }
    sort(names.begin(), names.end());
    sort(ages.begin(), ages.end());
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        cout << names[i] << " is " << ages[i] << " years old." << endl;
    }
    return 0;
}

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaximumX(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
        int m = matrix.size();
        int n = matrix[0].size();
        int maxX = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (matrix[i][j] > maxX) {
                    maxX = matrix[i][j];
                }
            }
        }
        return maxX;
    }
};

#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <map>
#include <set>
#include <algorithm>

using namespace std;

class Solution {
public:
    int findMaxForm(vector<int>& nums) {
        int max = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < nums.size(); i++) {
            if (nums[i] > max) {
                max = nums[i];
            }
        }
        return max;
    }
};

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    Solution solution;
    int maxForm = solution.findMaxForm(nums);
    cout << "Max form: " << maxForm << endl;
    return 0;
}

```

This is a solution to the problem "Find the maximum form of a given vector of integers". The solution uses a simple loop to iterate through the vector and checks if the current element is greater than the maximum element found so

import React from 'react';
import { useState } from 'react';
import axios from 'axios';

const API_URL = 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts';

function App() {
  const [posts, setPosts] = useState([]);

  const fetchPosts = async () => {
    try {
      const response = await axios.get(`${API_URL}`);
      setPosts(response.data);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(error);
    }
  };

  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Posts</h1>
      <ul>
        {posts.map((post) => (
          <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <button onClick={fetchPosts}>Fetch Posts</button>
    </div>
  );
}

export default App;

# Titanosaurus

Titanosaurus (meaning "Titan lizard") is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period, around 85 to 75 million years ago. The type and only species is Titanosaurus indicus. It was described in 1979 and is known from a nearly complete skeleton found in the Kutch District of Gujarat, India.

Titanosaurus was a very large sauropod, estimated to have reached lengths of around 30 meters (98 feet) and weighing around 100 metric tons (110 tons). It had a long, heavy body with a small head, a long neck, and a long tail. Its limbs were relatively short compared to its body size, and it had five clawed digits on each foot.

Titanosaurus is known for its unique skull and dental structure. Its skull was broad and flat, with a long, curved snout and a distinctive crest on the top of the skull. Its teeth were also distinctive, with a rounded crown and a distinctive root structure

Tips for a Successful Business Partnership
By: David G. Blank | 3,625 Reads | 1 Shares
A successful business partnership can be a powerful tool for growing and scaling a business. Here are some tips for building a successful partnership:
1. Define the partnership's purpose and goals.
2. Establish a clear division of responsibilities and roles.
3. Develop a shared vision and set of values.
4. Communicate openly and honestly.
5. Establish a system of checks and balances.
6. Foster a culture of trust and respect.
7. Be flexible and willing to adapt.
8. Have a plan for conflict resolution.
9. Set clear boundaries and expectations.
10. Have a written partnership agreement.
11. Regularly evaluate and assess the partnership.
12. Have a plan for succession and exit.
13. Be willing to compromise and find common ground.
14. Be transparent and honest in all dealings.
15. Respect each other's strengths and weaknesses.
